title: Tonalli Tec 10 Operations Summary - Q4 2018.pdf
doc_type: Quarterly operations report (Word export to PDF, 5 pages)
summary: Narrative Q4-2018 TEC-10 report: operating statement, how the price formula and royalties work, operating-cost structure, rent-vs-buy, NAFIN factoring, netback sensitivity to water cut and WTI. Text complete; the charts on pages 4-5 do not render.
key_data_with_units: Q4-2018: 13,489 bbl; revenue USD 811,642; RTF 337,225; opex 230,267; NOI 244,150; 60.17 USD/bbl price, 25.00 royalties, 17.07 opex, 18.10 netback. PEMEX under-charged the 3 % marketing fee in Sep-Oct 2018 (about USD 16 k credit note). C factor 0.916 at 28 API; PEMEX suggested API >= 30 might give C = 1. Taxes and fees MXN 9,273 + 12,095 = 21,368/month (USD 1,282); 'exploration phase' until the Evaluation Period ends and the Development Plan is approved, after which fees rise. Royalties due the 17th of the following month. Landowner royalty = 1 % of gross revenue less base and contract royalties, paid annually. Rent vs buy: USD 65 k vs 40 k/month. NAFIN factoring at an estimated 4-5 %/yr. TEC-10 break-even: WTI 50 at 72 % water cut, 60 at 78 %, 70 at 85 % (at about USD 65 k/month opex).
interpretation: Explains the fiscal regime and price formula in the operator's own words, and states that the fixed fees step up in the extraction phase, which supports G-60. The water-cut break-evens at 2018 rental-era costs (72-85 % water cut) are a useful benchmark: at the post-2020 cost base (about USD 28 k/month) break-even water cuts would be higher, but this report does not compute them.
use_in_presentation: Fiscal regime explainer; price formula; break-even vs water cut
repo_impact: confirms G-60 (extraction phase raises fees) and G-24 (formula, C factor); adds break-even water-cut sensitivity and landowner royalty definition (1 % of revenue net of royalties; the 2023 model uses 1 % of revenue + royalties)
